title: Prevention of hypoglycaemia in low birth weight newborns with oral 10% dextrose
author: Dominik Metz
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.qijducn
materials: Parental refusal to participate to the study OR
Birth weight less than 1500 g (VLBW) OR

Ethical Considerations We consider the intervention of 10% dextrose safe, as it has been used orally for different purposes (analgesic control) and there are no documented adverse effects, its use has also been recommended by international medical agencies (MSF). Further, in terms of glycemic control, there have been a few small trials in the use of oral dextrose that did not find any significant adverse effects (3). Considering the possibility that giving the baby supplemental feeding may reduce the amount of breast milk, we will encourage continuous breast milk stimulation and monitor time taken to establish feed. The participants will have their glucose monitored in both arms and a clear rescue plan is elaborated for all participants. The control arm are receiving no less than what low birth weight babies would normally receive in the context (breast milk). Furthermore they will be monitored stringently in terms of glucose levels as well as vital signs. All patient identifiable data will be removed from the data collection sheets. Data will be stored in a secure space with only researchers having access to it. All data collection sheets are anonymised to ensure patient confidentiality. The consent form is modelled on the World Health Organisation Consent form. Research staff will provide information to the participant guardians both verbally and in writing (Kiswahili). They will be encouraged to ask questions and discuss any issues. The researchers will be trained in gaining consent and the importance of the individuals right to decline participation in the study. The participant guardians will be given time to consider the proposal and encouraged to discuss with others as well as ask for clarification/ questions if needed. No pressure or coercion will be exerted to participate in the study. No financial incentives or gifts will be offered to participate in the study. Consent will then be obtained in writing- via signature or thumb print. If at any part of the study the participants guardian wish to withdraw from the trial they will be allowed to do so, and routine care will be continued, likewise, If consent is refused, routine care will be offered without prejudice. Comprehension of the information provided will be assessed using simple questions including "Can you explain to me what you understand so far?" . For patients with disabilities, we will assess capacity to make informed consent and involve relatives where appropriate.

steps.title: Screen and Enroll Participants
steps.instruction: Identify neonates in the first day of life who meet the inclusion and exclusion criteria and obtain parental consent.

substeps.instruction: Verify inclusion criteria: Birth weight <2500 g and parental consent.

Verify exclusion criteria: Parental refusal, major congenital malformations, birth weight <1500 g (VLBW), signs of significant respiratory distress syndrome (RR >80, grunting), or birth asphyxia (APGAR <7 at 10 minutes).
Obtain written informed consent in local language (Kiswahili) or English; use thumb print for signatures if the parent is unable to read.

steps.title: Randomize Participants
steps.instruction: Assign eligible babies to either the Dextrose (Arm D) or Control (Arm C) arm using a 1:1 computer-generated randomization list.

substeps.instruction: Maintain masking of clinicians, families, and investigators until enrollment.
Disclose arm allocation immediately after enrollment.

steps.title: Monitor Glucose and Vital Signs
steps.instruction: Perform regular monitoring of glucose levels, vital signs, and body weight for all participants.

substeps.instruction: Measure pre-feed glucose using Accu-Chek Active meter at 1, 3, 5, and 7 hours after birth, then every 4 hours for 2 days, and every 6 hours on the third day.
Monitor vital signs (respiratory rate, heart rate, and temperature) 2 times per day, or more frequently if abnormal.
Measure body weight at birth and daily thereafter.
Document all parameters on the separate pro-forma and data collection sheets.

steps.title: Implement Arm D (Dextrose Supplementation)
steps.instruction: Provide 2-hourly cup feeds using Expressed Breast Milk (EBM) supplemented with 10% dextrose to meet the optimal daily fluid requirement.

substeps.instruction: Calculate 2-hourly feed quantity based on daily requirements: Day 1 (60 ml/kg ÷ 12), Day 2 (80 ml/kg ÷ 12), and Day 3 (100 ml/kg ÷ 12).
Use 10ml and 20ml measuring cups/syringes to measure EBM and 10% dextrose.
Supplement with 10% dextrose if EBM amount is insufficient to reach the calculated volume.
Stop providing oral 10% dextrose once EBM production exceeds 70% of the daily fluid requirement, but continue recording milk quantity.
Use a timer to ensure feeds are administered every 2 hours.

steps.title: Implement Arm C (Control)
steps.instruction: Provide 2-hourly feeds consisting only of EBM.

substeps.instruction: Record the amount of EBM produced every 2 hours.
Use 10ml and 20ml measuring cups/syringes to measure EBM.

steps.title: Provide General Care
steps.instruction: Encourage additional breast feeding (BF) post-EBM and skin-to-skin contact for participants in both arms.

steps.title: Execute Rescue Plan
steps.instruction: Intervene based on glucose levels or clinical signs of complications.

substeps.instruction: If glucose < 2.6 mmol/L: Give immediate feed (required amount +/- 10% Dextrose) and recheck glucose 1 hour post-feed.
If glucose < 1.1 mmol/L: Administer 2 ml/kg IV 10% dextrose and recheck glucose in 1 hour.
If clinical signs of Necrotising Enterocolitis (vomiting, blood in stool, absent bowel sounds, abdominal distention) develop: Switch fluids to IV and commence antibiotics.
If signs of sepsis develop: Commence IV antibiotics (Ampicillin 50 mg/kg BD & Gentamicin 5 mg/kg OD).
If clinical signs of dehydration develop and EBM is insufficient: Provide oral or IV 10% dextrose based on clinical judgement.

steps.title: Manage Participant Withdrawal
steps.instruction: Remove participants from the trial and revert to routine neonatal care if the mother retracts consent or if significant/unforeseen side effects develop.

substeps.instruction: Document the withdrawal and share it with the safety monitoring group.
